explanation: In C++, when a class contains virtual functions, the compiler implements a vtable (virtual table) to enable dynamic dispatch at runtime. The vtable is an array of pointers to virtual functions, associated with each polymorphic object. Each object of such a class contains an implicit pointer (vptr) to its class's vtable, which the compiler initializes during object construction. When a virtual function is called through a base class pointer or reference, the program uses the vptr to locate the correct function in the vtable, ensuring the appropriate derived class implementation executes. This mechanism allows C++ to support runtime polymorphism efficiently, with the vtable acting as an internal lookup table for virtual function calls.
